name: tui-ssh
tagline: The SSH server as it really is, with every change previewed before it runs
description:
A terminal UI for the machine's SSH server. It asks sshd what its configuration actually is — `sshd -T`, not what a file says — and shows the settings that decide who gets in first, each with a verdict and the file and line that set it.

Five more screens complete the picture: who is logged in right now and a way to end a session; what the authentication log says over the last day or week; the host keys and their fingerprints; the unit and its sockets; and the local accounts with the keys that log into them, where one is added or removed.

Changes go to a drop-in: tui-ssh never rewrites /etc/ssh/sshd_config. It writes 90-tui-ssh.conf, checks the staged file with `sshd -t -f` before asking anything, and shows the diff and both commands. sshd takes the first value it is given, so the include order is read too: if another file already sets the keyword earlier, the tool says so instead of writing a line that would be ignored. A keyword can also go inside a `Match` block, which the file keeps last: sshd reads what follows one as part of it.

Run `tui-ssh --demo` to drive a sample server: every key works, every command is built and previewed for real, and nothing touches your system.

keys.action: Move between config, sessions, auth log, host keys, service and users
Open the selected row in full
Change the selected setting, written to a drop-in with a diff to confirm
Change a setting inside a Match block, for some connections only
Add a public key to an account's authorized_keys
Block the selected address at the firewall
Switch the log window between the last 24 hours and 7 days
Regenerate the server's host keys, old ones moved aside
Filter the rows of the current screen
On users, remove the selected key; on every other screen, re-read
Re-read the server, from any screen

notes.impact: `sshd -T` prints the canonical spelling of every keyword (`PermitRootLogin no`) where 10.2 and earlier lower-case it (`permitrootlogin no`); both forms are parsed to the canonical name, so the verdicts and the source lines are the same either way
the version comes from `ssh -V`, which prints to standard error; `sshd -V` only exists from OpenSSH 9.6, so asking the server itself would report nothing over most of the supported range
`Include` does not exist, so /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d is never read; tui-ssh will not rewrite sshd_config itself, so the editor has nowhere to write and says so
`KbdInteractiveAuthentication` is still spelled `ChallengeResponseAuthentication`; both are read, and the old name is what gets written

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-ssh/releases/download/v{version}/tui-ssh_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-ssh
sudo install -m0755 tui-ssh /usr/local/bin/tui-ssh
binary.note: One static binary. Verify it against checksums.txt from the same release.

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-ssh
cd tui-ssh && make build
sudo install -m0755 bin/tui-ssh /usr/local/bin/tui-ssh

security.needs_sudo: Two reads escalate through `sudo -n`, which never prompts: `sshd -T`, and `cat` for a file the plain read cannot open — sshd_config on Fedora and Arch, or another account's authorized_keys. Both fall back rather than demand a password, and the screen says so. Every change escalates too.
